newsitem.title: USA: FEATURE-Hanson emerge as pop's latest young sensations.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Hanson emerge as pop's latest young sensations.

text.p: Move over 14-year-old LeAnn Rimes and the three teenagers of Silverchair. The Hanson brothers from Tulsa, Oklahoma, are the latest youngsters to make a splash in the music world.

Their infectious first single "MMMBop" has just become the number one song in the United States after just four weeks in release, and their major-label debut album, "Middle of Nowhere," stands at nine in its first week on the Top 200.
Hanson consists of guitarist Isaac, 16, singer/keyboardist Taylor, 14, and drummer Zachary, 11. All are classically trained pianists, and they frequently swap instruments and vocal duties.

A combination of good looks and highly catchy tunes might draw comparisons with short-lived teen stars of the past, such as New Kids on the Block and Tiffany. But the brothers place their allegiance with icons from rock 'n' roll's early days.
"The stuff that we were really inspired by at the beginning was late '50s, early '60s rock 'n' roll," Isaac said in an interview with Reuters.

"People like Chuck Berry, the Supremes, Aretha Franklin. All the classic people that you can think of from that era of music was really a lot of the stuff that we listened to at the beginning of our career."

The seeds were sown early on when their father's job as a drilling contractor took the family overseas for long spells. "We didn't listen to the radio beause we didn't understand it, so we had Time-Life tapes," Taylor says.

Those mail-order compilations of classic rock and soul songs led the brothers to delve deeper into music. They performed publicly for the first time five years ago as an a capella trio at an arts festival in Tulsa.
HELP FROM AN OLD LUDWIG DRUM SET

Two years after that, they came across an old Ludwig drum set, to which Zachary took a shine. Isaac picked up a guitar at a pawn shop, and they began phase two of their career by going on the road and playing schools.
This was facilitated by the fact that they are home-schooled. But Isaac stresses that they have not been pushed into showbiz by over-eager parents.

"Our parents have been really good about just supporting us in general," he says. "'Guys, if you want to stop, we'll stop. If you want to keep going and push harder, let's push harder.' They've just been there to back us up."
With two independent albums to their credit, Hanson signed to Mercury Records last year and spent six months in Los Angeles making "Middle of Nowhere."
They have sole songwriting credit on three songs, including "MMMBop," and share the credit on the rest with such big guns as Barry Mann and Cynthia Weil, Mark Hudson and Desmond Child.
UPBEAT ALBUM
Zachary astutely ascribes the album's upbeat, Motown-ish nature to the fact that "we don't have as many problems" as grown-ups.
But Isaac is quick to point out that the band is completely serious about its music.

"We're not a novelty act, and we don't plan to be. I'm sure people will say that. It's just their perception of it. We love to make music, we love doing what we're doing. We love where we are, and we want to keep doing that in our lives."
Indeed, the album cleverly mixes hilarity with serious themes. Behind the dance friendly "MMMBop" is a story about fostering lasting relationships.
"With You In Your Dreams" was written while their grandmother was dying, and "Yearbook Song" invents a story about a kid whose photo didn't appear in the high school yearbook.
"Even though being a kid is kind of a carefree sort of thing for the most part, I guess, there are definitely a lot of things that stick in kids' minds," Isaac says.
THEY GET ALONG FOR NOW

For the time being, the brothers get along with each other, and with their parents and three younger siblings. Taylor is shy and likes literature; Isaac alternates between calmness and frenzied activity, and he has been writing a science fiction novel for the past two years. By common agreement, the math-loving Zachary is the unabashed crazy one.
"I think it's probably actually that I'm so shy that I just act wacky to make up," he says.

"He's dragged people up on stage," says Taylor. "We would give T-shirts away. This one girl raised her hand, but she was too embarrassed to come up, so he went out there and carried her onto the stage."

Which raises the subject of how the band deals with fame and fans at such a young age. Zachary is already beginning to sound jaded, saying, "You can't avoid getting girls if you're a guy (in a band)."
More importantly, the brothers say they are looking to soak up as much knowledge as they can from their showbiz travails.
"It's all very much a learning experience," Isaac says. "With every experience, you try to learn a little bit more about what you're doing, and try to do your job better."
